title: Congruent figures
summary: Recognise congruent figures and use corresponding equal sides and angles.
objectives: Recognise figures with identical shape and size.
Match corresponding vertices, sides and angles.
Apply SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS congruence criteria.

blocks.text: Congruent figures can be mapped exactly onto one another by translations, rotations or reflections. Their corresponding sides and angles are equal; orientation may differ.

Congruent figures have identical shape and size even after translation, rotation or reflection. Write corresponding vertices in matching order. Equal tick marks identify corresponding sides and equal arc marks identify corresponding angles.

For triangles, SSS uses three side pairs, SAS uses two sides and their included angle, ASA uses two angles and the included side, and RHS applies to right triangles with equal hypotenuse and one corresponding side. AAA proves similarity, not congruence; SSA is generally insufficient.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: Congruent triangles have corresponding sides 3x + 1 cm and 16 cm. Find x.

sections.verification_note: Check that every side and angle was matched in the stated corresponding order.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: Right triangles ABC and PQR have right angles at B and Q, AC=PR=13 cm and AB=PQ=5 cm. Prove the triangles congruent and find the remaining side.

content.text: AC and PR are equal hypotenuses, AB and PQ are equal corresponding sides, and both triangles are right-angled.
Therefore the triangles are congruent by RHS.
Using Pythagoras, the remaining side is √(13²−5²)=12 cm in each triangle.

sections.verification_note: The correspondence A↔P, B↔Q, C↔R preserves the right angle, hypotenuse and matching side.

blocks.text: Do not use AAA for congruence. In SAS, the equal angle must lie between the two equal sides. State the vertex correspondence before transferring a side or angle from one triangle to the other.

prompt.text: A triangle is reflected. Use code 1 if the image must be congruent and code 0 otherwise.

feedback.text: A reflection preserves every length and angle, so the image is congruent.

blocks.text: Write the correspondence first, use one consistent scale factor, preserve equal angles, and check whether a length, perimeter or area needs a linear or squared factor.
Before moving on, explain the relevant property in words, show the equation or formula with units, and use the diagram markings to check that every correspondence is consistent.
